messages:
aj: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression on staging after the batcher change in PR 0x4f2a. 99th pct latency jumped ~3x for short requests. attaching nsys timeline next.

maria: saw that too. started an nsys capture on a repro load. timeline shows a tight loop of tiny kernels labeled `kv_cache_lookup` + a bunch of tiny `matmul` invocations between, lots of kernel launch overhead.

maria: paste of the hot part from the timeline (condensed):
```
[GPU Timeline]
0 ms: launch attn_fwd
0.1 ms: kv_cache_lookup (0.02 ms)
0.12 ms: matmul_small (0.01 ms)
0.13 ms: kv_cache_lookup (0.02 ms)
0.15 ms: memcpy H2D (sync)
...
```

ethan: can you attach the capture/command? I'll run locally.

maria: command I ran:
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/trace --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --sample=none --capture-range=process:12345 --force-overwrite --section=nvtx ./bench_runner --config short-reqs.json
```

simon: quick theory: the batcher used to accumulate small requests for ~2ms and now default's 0ms so flushes immediately => many tiny kernels. nsys shows kernel ramp-up overhead dominating.

nish: that change was in batcher heuristics commit 0x4f2a? IIRC we switched from `flush_delay_ms: 2` -> `0` to reduce tail latency for chat workloads.

aj: yes 0x4f2a touched batcher flush and also touched the KV cache lookup path to remove coalescing. suspect both.

benchbot: perf run summary (staging, 1k short requests):
```
baseline (before 0x4f2a): p99=42ms, p50=9ms
after 0x4f2a: p99=136ms, p50=11ms
GPU kernel time per-request increased by ~2.5x, but total GPU compute is similar -> overhead + launch latency.
```

ethan: sounds like a good bisect target. We should isolate whether it's the batcher flush change or the KV coalescing removal.

simon: I can bisect. plan:
- revert only batcher flush change, run short-req benchmark + nsys
- revert only KV-coalesce change, run again
- compare timelines: look for reduction in kernel-launch counts and larger fused kernels

maria: adding reproduction steps (lightweight):
1) start bench_runner with concurrent 80 clients, short prompt (~8 tokens)
2) run nsys with capture-range=process
3) export timeline and grep for `kv_cache_lookup` occurrences

maria: small log snippet showing repeated tiny launches:
```
I0321 14:02:11.123 kernel_launch: kv_cache_lookup size=128 exec=23us
I0321 14:02:11.125 kernel_launch: matmul_small size=64 exec=10us
I0321 14:02:11.127 kernel_launch: kv_cache_lookup size=128 exec=21us
```

aj: i tried reverting batcher delay locally to 2ms and the p99 dropped to ~48ms. so batcher change is main culprit but KV changes still look noisy.

nish: ok that's helpful. do we want a temporary config to make flush_delay configurable per-deployment? could ship that while we bisect the other change.

ethan: agreed. patch to expose `flush_delay_ms` in runtime config would be quick.

simon: bisect results so far (in-progress):
- 0x4f2a (batcher+kv): regressed
- 0x4e9f (batcher only): regressed
- 0x4e2d (kv-only): minor/noise

simon: conclusion so far: batcher flush change accounts for most of the regression. KV coalescing removal adds some extra kernel chatter but not main driver.

maria: one more interesting find: perfetto capture shows large idle gaps on GPU between tiny kernels, suggesting launch overhead and CPU scheduling causing stalls.

maria: screenshot of flame-ish view: https://infraprod/imgs/1862/kv-nsys-smallkernels.png

aj: i'll open a PR to revert the batcher behavior and add a config flag. will include benchmark runs.

benchbot: note: if we revert, watch memory/cold-cache behavior for long-seq workloads — we previously increased flush to avoid too much batching on long sequences.

nish: good call. let's gate revert behind a config toggle and enable by default to previous value for staging. roll forward carefully to prod.

ethan: after revert PR, we'll run full regression harness and post nsys comparisons (before/after). I can automate diff-ing kernel counts and launch times.

maria: thanks all. tagging perf-owners: @ethan @simon. if anyone has spare cycles pls help with automated timeline diff script.

aj: will follow up with PR link and timeline diffs once CI finishes. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: automated perf job queued: job/8342 — will post results here when done.
